elements.content: Grammar focus: Advanced Hedging & Academic Stance Devices.

Core Rule: Use distance verbs ( appear to, tend to, suggest ), probability adverbs ( arguably, conceivably, presumably ), and modal past structures ( would seem to indicate ) to avoid overgeneralization.

Probability Adverbs — arguably / conceivably / presumably: The policy is arguably the most effective intervention to date.
Distance Verbs — appear to / tend to / suggest: The preliminary findings tend to suggest a gradual shift.
Modal Past Expressions — would seem to + Base / Have V3: The preliminary dataset would seem to indicate structural change.
Noun Hedging Phrases — There is reason to believe that...: There is reason to believe that regulatory updates will follow.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence demonstrates appropriate academic hedging?
options: The findings would seem to indicate a positive trend.
The findings prove without question that we are 100% correct.

elements.content: 2. Choose the hedged probability adverb:
Read and listen: three examples in context.

The results suggest that sleep matters.
This may indicate a trend.
It appears that the method works.
The effect is likely to be small.
1. Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Advanced Hedging & Academic Stance Devices?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
